findings.issue_text: ErrDeviceLimitReached masks 'device not found' and blocks legitimate first-time and returning users: rowsAffected == 0 is returned both when the device doesn't exist in the window and when the UPDATE was a no-op, so once the cap is hit every brand-new anonymous device fails CreateOrUpdateDevice, breaking anonymous authentication for new users entirely

MySQL no-op UPDATE returns RowsAffected() == 0 for matching rows with unchanged values: a known, in-window device re-tagging with the same values (e.g., same updated_at) can spuriously trigger ErrDeviceLimitReached and fail auth for an existing device

Count-then-act is not atomic: CountDevices and the subsequent insert run in separate transactions, so concurrent anonymous requests can each read count < limit and all insert, exceeding the limit (TOCTOU hole)

Blocking DB write moved onto the synchronous auth path with no timeout: TagDevice now runs synchronously using the request's context instead of a background goroutine with 2-minute timeout, adding DB latency to every anonymous request, and the removed panic-recovery means a tagging panic crashes the auth path
TagDevice error contract change breaks other callers silently: it previously logged UI-tag failures and returned nil, now returns the error, potentially breaking callers not updated in this diff

Type mismatch: Go always serializes AnonymousDeviceLimit as an integer (never undefined) while frontend types it as number | undefined, making the 'unset' sentinel impossible and the union type misleading

TOCTOU race in CreateOrUpdateDevice: CountDevices limit check and insert are separate non-transactional queries, allowing concurrent anonymous requests to blow past the device limit; needs a conditional insert or transactional bounded upsert
Authentication path now synchronously blocked on a DB write: TagDevice is called inline in Authenticate instead of a fire-and-forget goroutine, so slow/degraded database stalls all anonymous access
Panic recovery dropped from device tagging path, so a panic in tagging now propagates into the auth request

Expired devices older than 30 days can never be updated, and slot reclamation depends on DeleteDevicesOlderThan job running; if unscheduled, new/returning devices are permanently locked out and the interplay is undocumented
ErrDeviceLimitReached conflates 'limit reached' with 'device_id doesn't exist' since rowsAffected == 0, risking misclassification by future callers
ErrDeviceLimitReached error is not wrapped with context (no device id), making log debugging difficult
Local cache only dedupes the same device (29 min TTL) but does not rate-limit distinct devices, leaving the TOCTOU limit race fully exposed to anonymous traffic

Per-request COUNT query on hot anonymous-auth path: CreateOrUpdateDevice runs CountDevices with updated_at BETWEEN range over the whole anon_device table on every tagged request when deviceLimit > 0, potentially a full table scan per anonymous request

TagDevice moved from async background goroutine to synchronous request path in Authenticate, adding two synchronous DB round trips to anonymous auth latency and using request context that cancels on client disconnect
Count-then-update TOCTOU race: CountDevices check and subsequent write are not in one transaction, so concurrent requests can all observe count < limit and overshoot the configured device limit

updateDevice treats any zero-row update as ErrDeviceLimitReached, so returning devices with updated_at older than 30 days (or missing devices due to the race) cause legitimate returning visitors to be hard-failed on auth

DB write (TagDevice) moved onto the synchronous auth path in client.go Authenticate: every uncached anonymous request now pays a CountDevices query plus an insert/update, degrading auth latency when DB is slow

TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit gives false confidence: ErrDeviceLimitReached is returned because the UPDATE matched 0 rows, not because the limit path was exercised, so the test passes even if updateDevice unconditionally fails

Returning raw ErrDeviceLimitReached from Authenticate surfaces as a generic auth failure (likely 500/401) instead of a 429 throttling response, with no backoff or distinct status for over-limit devices

adjudication_records.issue_text: ErrDeviceLimitReached masks 'device not found' and blocks legitimate first-time and returning users: rowsAffected == 0 is returned both when the device doesn't exist in the window and when the UPDATE was a no-op, so once the cap is hit every brand-new anonymous device fails CreateOrUpdateDevice, breaking anonymous authentication for new users entirely

MySQL no-op UPDATE returns RowsAffected() == 0 for matching rows with unchanged values: a known, in-window device re-tagging with the same values (e.g., same updated_at) can spuriously trigger ErrDeviceLimitReached and fail auth for an existing device

adjudication.rationale: In `updateDevice`, the code treats `RowsAffected()==0` as `ErrDeviceLimitReached` (and `Anonymous.Authenticate` returns the error, failing auth). But the UPDATE can legitimately match an existing row while reporting 0 affected rows when the SET values don’t change (a known MySQL behavior: affected rows counts changed rows, not matched rows). Since the UPDATE sets `client_ip`, `user_agent`, and `updated_at` from the incoming `device` (`updated_at=?`), re-tagging an existing device with the same persisted values (e.g., same `updated_at` due to timestamp precision/truncation or identical inputs) would spuriously produce `RowsAffected()==0` and incorrectly trigger `ErrDeviceLimitReached` even though the device exists and is within the allowed window.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Count-then-act is not atomic: CountDevices and the subsequent insert run in separate transactions, so concurrent anonymous requests can each read count < limit and all insert, exceeding the limit (TOCTOU hole)

Blocking DB write moved onto the synchronous auth path with no timeout: TagDevice now runs synchronously using the request's context instead of a background goroutine with 2-minute timeout, adding DB latency to every anonymous request, and the removed panic-recovery means a tagging panic crashes the auth path

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that Anonymous.Authenticate no longer tags the device in a background goroutine with a dedicated 2-minute timeout and local panic-recovery. In pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go the goroutine, context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), timeoutTag), and recover() wrapper were removed, and TagDevice is now called synchronously with the passed-in ctx: `if err := a.anonDeviceService.TagDevice(ctx, httpReqCopy, ...)`. Since TagDevice ultimately performs store writes (anonstore DB usage), this can add DB latency onto the synchronous auth path, and there is no longer a local panic guard in Authenticate. Whether a panic would "crash" the auth path depends on higher-level recovery not shown in the diff, so that portion is not fully verifiable here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TagDevice error contract change breaks other callers silently: it previously logged UI-tag failures and returned nil, now returns the error, potentially breaking callers not updated in this diff

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a behavioral/API contract change in `AnonDeviceService.TagDevice`: on UI tagging failure it now returns the error (`impl.go`: after `a.tagDeviceUI(...)`, it logs and `return err`), whereas previously it logged the failure and continued returning `nil`. That is a real, diff-grounded change that can affect any existing callers expecting TagDevice to be best-effort. However, the claim that it "breaks other callers" beyond those updated here isn’t verifiable from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Type mismatch: Go always serializes AnonymousDeviceLimit as an integer (never undefined) while frontend types it as number | undefined, making the 'unset' sentinel impossible and the union type misleading

adjudication.rationale: Diff shows backend always includes `anonymousDeviceLimit` as a non-omitempty `int64` (`FrontendSettingsDTO.AnonymousDeviceLimit int64` and `hs.Cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit`, defaulted via `MustInt64(0)`), so JSON will always contain a number (typically 0 when unset). Frontend types it as `number | undefined` and boot config initializes it to `undefined`, which doesn’t match what this backend will ever send; if `undefined` was meant as an “unset” sentinel, it can’t occur with the current Go DTO. This is a type/contract mismatch but not a demonstrated runtime defect in the diff (0 is a valid sentinel in the Go logic: `deviceLimit > 0`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: TOCTOU race in CreateOrUpdateDevice: CountDevices limit check and insert are separate non-transactional queries, allowing concurrent anonymous requests to blow past the device limit; needs a conditional insert or transactional bounded upsert

adjudication.rationale: In `CreateOrUpdateDevice`, the device limit enforcement does `CountDevices(...)` and then (if under limit) proceeds to an insert/upsert as a separate operation, without a shared transaction/lock across both steps. Under concurrent requests, multiple goroutines can observe `count < deviceLimit` and all insert, exceeding the configured limit. The diff shows no transactional wrapper spanning the count+write, so the TOCTOU race described is a real correctness issue in the newly added limit logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Authentication path now synchronously blocked on a DB write: TagDevice is called inline in Authenticate instead of a fire-and-forget goroutine, so slow/degraded database stalls all anonymous access

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `Authenticate` no longer tags the anon device in a fire-and-forget goroutine with its own timeout. In `pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go`, the previous `go func(){ ... context.WithTimeout(...); a.anonDeviceService.TagDevice(...) }()` block was removed and replaced with a direct `a.anonDeviceService.TagDevice(ctx, ...)` call. Since `TagDevice` ultimately calls into the anon store (DB-backed, e.g. `CreateOrUpdateDevice` in `anonstore/database.go`), this makes the authentication request path wait on that work. Even though non-limit errors are only logged (and auth still succeeds), a slow/degraded DB can still synchronously delay anonymous requests. This is a real, diff-grounded availability/perf concern, but it may be an intentional tradeoff to enforce `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, so it’s not conclusively a correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Panic recovery dropped from device tagging path, so a panic in tagging now propagates into the auth request

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the goroutine wrapper and its `defer`/`recover` in `Anonymous.Authenticate` (previously guarding `anonDeviceService.TagDevice(...)`). It is now called inline without any panic recovery, so a panic inside `TagDevice` (or deeper) would propagate up the auth request path instead of being contained/logged as before. This is a real robustness/regression concern grounded in the change, though it’s not provably a concrete defect without evidence that `TagDevice` can panic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Expired devices older than 30 days can never be updated, and slot reclamation depends on DeleteDevicesOlderThan job running; if unscheduled, new/returning devices are permanently locked out and the interplay is undocumented

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not support the claim that expired (>30d) devices “can never be updated” or that slot reclamation depends on DeleteDevicesOlderThan. In CreateOrUpdateDevice, the special updateDevice path is only taken when deviceLimit>0 AND CountDevices(now-30d..now+1m) >= deviceLimit; otherwise it falls through to the normal upsert logic (which would update an existing device regardless of age). Also, reclamation of capacity is based on CountDevices only counting the last 30 days (old rows don’t consume the limit even if not deleted), so it doesn’t depend on a deletion job being scheduled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ErrDeviceLimitReached conflates 'limit reached' with 'device_id doesn't exist' since rowsAffected == 0, risking misclassification by future callers

adjudication.rationale: In `updateDevice`, `rowsAffected == 0` causes `ErrDeviceLimitReached` to be returned even though `0` rows can also mean the `device_id` doesn’t exist or the `updated_at BETWEEN ? AND ?` predicate didn’t match (`pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go`). This makes the error semantically ambiguous and could mislead future callers who interpret `ErrDeviceLimitReached` as strictly “limit hit”, even though it’s also used as “no eligible row to update.”

adjudication_records.issue_text: ErrDeviceLimitReached error is not wrapped with context (no device id), making log debugging difficult

adjudication.rationale: The diff defines a sentinel error `var ErrDeviceLimitReached = fmt.Errorf("device limit reached")` in `pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go` and returns it from `updateDevice()` when `rowsAffected == 0`. This error carries no contextual information (e.g., `device.DeviceID`) and is propagated up to `client.go`, where `errors.Is(err, anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached)` causes an early return without any logging. That makes diagnosing which device hit the limit harder, but it’s an observability/debuggability issue rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Local cache only dedupes the same device (29 min TTL) but does not rate-limit distinct devices, leaving the TOCTOU limit race fully exposed to anonymous traffic

adjudication.rationale: The new device-limit enforcement in `AnonDBStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice` is a classic TOCTOU check: it calls `CountDevices(...)` and, if below `s.deviceLimit`, proceeds to insert/upsert without any transactional guard (no lock/unique constraint-based limit). Under concurrent anonymous traffic with distinct `device_id`s, multiple requests can observe `count < limit` and all insert, exceeding the configured limit. The finding’s mention of the local cache isn’t necessary to verify the issue: the diff shows the limit check itself is race-prone and thus not reliably enforced.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Per-request COUNT query on hot anonymous-auth path: CreateOrUpdateDevice runs CountDevices with updated_at BETWEEN range over the whole anon_device table on every tagged request when deviceLimit > 0, potentially a full table scan per anonymous request

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a per-call device limit check in `AnonDBStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice`: when `s.deviceLimit > 0` it always calls `s.CountDevices(ctx, now-30d, now+1m)` before deciding to insert/update (`pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go`). Since `CreateOrUpdateDevice` is invoked from anonymous tagging (`TagDevice`), this introduces an extra COUNT query on that path whenever the limit is enabled. Whether it becomes a full table scan depends on DB indexing/schema not shown in the diff, so the "full scan" part is not strictly verifiable, but the potentially expensive per-request COUNT query is real and review-relevant.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TagDevice moved from async background goroutine to synchronous request path in Authenticate, adding two synchronous DB round trips to anonymous auth latency and using request context that cancels on client disconnect

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows TagDevice was changed from an async goroutine with a detached background context + timeout (removed `go func(){... context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), timeoutTag) ...}`) to a synchronous call in `Authenticate` (`a.anonDeviceService.TagDevice(ctx, ...)`). This can add work to the request path and now uses the passed `ctx` (likely request-scoped), so tagging may be canceled if the client disconnects. Also, `CreateOrUpdateDevice` can now do an extra `CountDevices` query before updating/inserting when `deviceLimit > 0`, increasing potential synchronous DB work in the auth path. This is a concrete performance/behavior-change concern, but not a clearly verifiable correctness defect from the diff alone.

However, the claim that it is "unbounded" or will "crash the request handler" is not fully verifiable from the diff alone (request context/middleware recovery are outside the diff), so this is best treated as a concrete performance/availability/architecture concern rather than a provable functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Count-then-insert race in CreateOrUpdateDevice: the device limit check uses CountDevices followed by a separate insert with no transaction, row lock, or unique constraint, allowing concurrent requests to overshoot the device limit

adjudication.rationale: In `CreateOrUpdateDevice`, the new limit enforcement does `CountDevices(...)` and, if `count < s.deviceLimit`, proceeds to the normal create/upsert path without any transaction/locking around the count+insert sequence (`pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go`). Under concurrent requests, multiple goroutines can observe `count` below the limit and both insert, causing the stored device count to exceed `deviceLimit`. The diff shows no row lock, serialized transaction, or other atomic mechanism to prevent this overshoot.

adjudication_records.issue_text: updateDevice conflates rowsAffected == 0 with ErrDeviceLimitReached, but zero rows can also occur when the device's updated_at falls outside the -30d/+1min window (clock skew or row cleanup), spuriously rejecting legitimate returning devices; additionally ErrDeviceLimitReached lacks visible HTTP status mapping so users may get a generic 500/401
matched_golden_ids: The updateDevice function returns ErrDeviceLimitReached when rowsAffected == 0, but zero affected rows means the device doesn't exist or falls outside the time window, not that a limit was reached.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same core bug: updateDevice treats rowsAffected == 0 as ErrDeviceLimitReached, but 0 affected rows can mean the device doesn’t exist or doesn’t match the time-window predicate (e.g., updated_at outside the -30d/+1min window), so the limit error is incorrect. Extra notes about HTTP status mapping are additional but don’t change the match.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Transient DB errors in TagDevice now fail anonymous requests where they previously succeeded, since tagDeviceUI errors previously were swallowed and logged asynchronously (graceful degradation via goroutine + warn log) has been removed

adjudication.rationale: In `pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go`, `Authenticate` no longer tags in a goroutine, but it still **does not fail anonymous auth on general TagDevice errors**: it only returns an error when `errors.Is(err, anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached)`; otherwise it just logs a warning and continues returning an anonymous identity. Although `TagDevice` in `impl.go` now returns the `tagDeviceUI` error (previously just logged), that error is still swallowed by `Authenticate` unless it’s `ErrDeviceLimitReached`. So transient DB errors would still not fail anonymous requests per the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Frontend settings contract mismatch: backend always emits anonymousDeviceLimit as int64 (including 0 when unset), but frontend types it as number | undefined with default undefined, so consumers checking !== undefined incorrectly treat 0 as configured

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a contract/type mismatch: backend `FrontendSettingsDTO` adds `AnonymousDeviceLimit int64 `json:"anonymousDeviceLimit"`` without `omitempty`, and it is always set from `hs.Cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit`, which defaults to `0` via `MustInt64(0)` in `readAuthSettings`. So the backend will always emit a numeric value (0 when unset). Frontend config types add `anonymousDeviceLimit: number | undefined` and `GrafanaBootConfig` defaults it to `undefined`, implying absence is meaningful. This can lead to incorrect frontend checks based on `undefined` vs `0`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit doesn't exercise the intended path: it only proves ErrDeviceLimitReached for a nonexistent device, never testing that a returning known device is updated successfully under the limit

adjudication.rationale: In `TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit`, after inserting the first device, the test changes `DeviceID` to a new value (`"keep"`) and expects `ErrDeviceLimitReached`. That exercises the `count >= deviceLimit` branch in `CreateOrUpdateDevice` and the failure case in `updateDevice` when `RowsAffected()==0` (i.e., the device does not already exist). It does not test the intended “returning known device” path where, once the limit is reached, calling `CreateOrUpdateDevice` with the *same* `DeviceID` should successfully update via `updateDevice` (rows affected > 0). This is a concrete test coverage gap for the newly added limit/update behavior, not a demonstrated defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test for auth-blocking behavior in Authenticate: no test calls Authenticate with a store at/over the device limit asserting ErrDeviceLimitReached is returned, nor that other TagDevice errors are swallowed and login succeeds

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `Anonymous.Authenticate` to call `a.anonDeviceService.TagDevice(ctx, ...)` synchronously and to *return* an error when `errors.Is(err, anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached)` (see `pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go`). Existing added/updated tests cover the store-level limit (`TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit` in `anonstore/database_test.go`) and TagDevice behavior (`anonimpl/impl_test.go`), but there is no test that exercises `Authenticate` with the device limit reached to assert it returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, nor a test asserting that non-limit `TagDevice` errors are logged/swallowed and authentication still succeeds. This is a specific missing test for newly added auth-blocking logic rather than a proven defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit only covers the failure branch of updateDevice; the happy path of a returning known device being updated at the limit is untested, leaving the UPDATE ... BETWEEN window logic (including +time.Minute upper bound and -30d lower bound) unverified

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial limit-handling logic in `AnonDBStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice`: when `count >= s.deviceLimit`, it calls `s.updateDevice(...)`, which runs an `UPDATE ... WHERE device_id = ? AND updated_at BETWEEN ? AND ?` using a `-anonymousDeviceExpiration` lower bound and a `+time.Minute` upper bound. The new test `TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit` only covers the case where the device is unknown at the limit (second call uses a new `DeviceID`), which results in `rowsAffected == 0` and returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached`. There is no test that, at the limit, an already-existing device ID is successfully updated (rowsAffected > 0), so the BETWEEN-window logic and the `+time.Minute`/`-30d` bounds are not verified by tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test for device_limit ini parsing/config wiring: no pkg/setting test asserting default of 0 (limit disabled), negative/unset values, and value propagation

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new ini-backed setting `auth.anonymous.device_limit` (`cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit = anonSection.Key("device_limit").MustInt64(0)`) and wires it into runtime behavior (`anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore(sqlStore, cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit)` plus frontend settings DTO/config). While there are integration tests for DB behavior at the limit (`TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit`), the diff shows no tests covering ini parsing defaults/unset/negative values or verifying config propagation from `setting.readAuthSettings` into `hs.Cfg`/frontend settings and the anon store construction.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Behavioral change (synchronous TagDevice + error propagation) with no test: TagDevice changed from fire-and-forget goroutine to synchronous and tagDeviceUI errors now propagate, but tests don't assert TagDevice returns an error on store failure or test removal of timeout/panic-recovery goroutine behavior

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes anonymous client behavior from an async, timeout-wrapped goroutine with panic recovery to a synchronous call (`client.go` removes the goroutine/timeout and calls `a.anonDeviceService.TagDevice(ctx, ...)` directly). It also changes `AnonDeviceService.TagDevice` to propagate `tagDeviceUI` errors (`impl.go` adds `return err` after logging). Existing integration tests still only assert `TagDevice` succeeds in normal cases and do not cover the new error-propagation path or failure scenarios (e.g., store/tagDeviceUI error, or the removed timeout/panic-recovery behavior), so the finding about missing tests for this nontrivial behavioral change is grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test that anonymousDeviceLimit reaches the frontend: no frontend settings test asserts the field is serialized, or pins whether a limit of 0 is sent (Go type int64 vs TS type number | undefined)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new frontend-facing field end-to-end (Go: `FrontendSettingsDTO.AnonymousDeviceLimit int64` with `json:"anonymousDeviceLimit"`, populated in `getFrontendSettings` from `hs.Cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit`; TS: `GrafanaConfig.anonymousDeviceLimit: number | undefined`, runtime default `undefined`). However, the only added/modified tests are for the anon DB store and anon device service; there is no test in this diff that asserts the frontend settings JSON includes `anonymousDeviceLimit` or clarifies the intended zero/undefined behavior given Go’s non-optional `int64` vs TS `number | undefined`. This is a specific, diff-grounded missing coverage for a new serialized contract, not a directly verifiable runtime defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No concurrency test for the count-then-insert race in CreateOrUpdateDevice: CountDevices followed by insert/update is non-atomic (TOCTOU), allowing the limit to be exceeded under concurrent anonymous requests, with no test documenting the intended semantics

adjudication.rationale: In `CreateOrUpdateDevice` (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go), the device limit enforcement is implemented as a non-atomic check-then-act sequence: it calls `CountDevices(...)` and, only if `count >= s.deviceLimit`, it switches to `updateDevice`; otherwise it proceeds to the normal insert/upsert path. Under concurrent requests, multiple goroutines can observe `count < limit` and all proceed to insert, exceeding the intended limit (classic TOCTOU race). There is no locking/transactional mechanism in the diff to make the count+insert atomic, and the added test (`TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit`) only exercises the sequential case, not the concurrent semantics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Anonymous device limit enforcement is not atomic: CountDevices followed by a separate insert allows concurrent requests to all pass the count check and exceed the limit (check-then-act race, no unique constraint, transaction, or locking in CreateOrUpdateDevice)

adjudication.rationale: In `CreateOrUpdateDevice` (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go), the limit check does `CountDevices(...)` and, only if `count >= s.deviceLimit`, switches to `s.updateDevice(...)`; otherwise it proceeds to the normal insert/upsert path. This is a classic check-then-act race: concurrent requests can both observe `count < deviceLimit` and then both insert, exceeding the limit. The diff shows no transaction spanning the count + insert, no locking, and no DB constraint/atomic conditional insert to enforce the limit.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Anonymous auth fails hard when limit is reached even for previously-seen devices: updateDevice only matches rows with updated_at within the 30-day/1-minute window while CountDevices gates on a different timestamp column, so a returning device with stale updated_at is counted toward the limit but fails the update and gets locked out

adjudication.rationale: When the device limit is reached, `CreateOrUpdateDevice` stops inserting and calls `updateDevice` instead (see `CreateOrUpdateDevice` in `anonstore/database.go`). But `updateDevice` only updates rows whose existing `updated_at` is within `[now-30d, now+1m]` (`WHERE device_id = ? AND updated_at BETWEEN ? AND ?`). If a device exists but its stored `updated_at` is older than 30 days, the UPDATE affects 0 rows and `updateDevice` returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached`. In `anonimpl/client.go`, `Authenticate` now treats `ErrDeviceLimitReached` as fatal (`return nil, err`), so anonymous auth can fail hard for a previously-known device record that is just stale. The finding’s specific claim about CountDevices using a different timestamp column isn’t verifiable from this diff, but the lockout behavior due to the UPDATE window is.

adjudication_records.issue_text: DB write (TagDevice) moved onto the synchronous auth path in client.go Authenticate: every uncached anonymous request now pays a CountDevices query plus an insert/update, degrading auth latency when DB is slow

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows TagDevice was changed from an async goroutine with its own timeout context to a synchronous call on the auth path (`client.go` Authenticate removed the `go func` and now calls `a.anonDeviceService.TagDevice(ctx, ...)` directly). That can directly add DB latency to authentication. Additionally, `CreateOrUpdateDevice` in `anonstore/database.go` now performs a `CountDevices(...)` query before insert/update when `deviceLimit > 0`, so with `cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit` configured (>0) each uncached tagging can pay an extra read plus a write. However, the finding overstates it as happening on “every” request: the count only happens when `deviceLimit > 0` (default is `0` via `MustInt64(0)`), and tagging may be skipped by the local cache (not shown in this diff).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Panic recovery was dropped when TagDevice moved inline: any panic inside TagDevice now propagates into Authenticate instead of being swallowed

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go, the previous goroutine wrapper around TagDevice included a defer/recover that swallowed panics and logged a warning. The new code calls a.anonDeviceService.TagDevice(ctx, ...) inline with no recover, so any panic inside TagDevice would now propagate up through Authenticate (subject to any higher-level middleware not shown in the diff). This is a concrete behavior/resilience change visible in the diff, but the diff does not prove TagDevice will panic, so it’s not a verifiable defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ErrDeviceLimitReached is a misleading sentinel for rowsAffected == 0 in updateDevice: it can also indicate clock skew or an absent device, so benign data mismatches are presented as policy rejections with no distinct signal

adjudication.rationale: In `updateDevice`, `rowsAffected == 0` is mapped to `ErrDeviceLimitReached` even though it can occur for reasons other than the policy limit (e.g., device_id not found, or `updated_at` not matching the `BETWEEN` window). This matters because when the limit is reached, `CreateOrUpdateDevice` calls `updateDevice`, and `Authenticate` treats `ErrDeviceLimitReached` as a hard failure (`return nil, err`). Thus benign data mismatches can be surfaced as a “device limit reached” policy rejection and can incorrectly block auth for an existing device that simply didn’t match the WHERE clause.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Frontend config type/serialization mismatch: backend always serializes anonymousDeviceLimit as a number (0 = unlimited) while frontend types allow undefined, making 0 and unset indistinguishable to consumers

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a real mismatch: the frontend config type declares `anonymousDeviceLimit: number | undefined` (grafana-data `GrafanaConfig`, and runtime boot config initializes it to `undefined`), while the backend DTO uses a non-optional `int64` field (`AnonymousDeviceLimit int64 `json:"anonymousDeviceLimit"``) and always populates it from `hs.Cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit`, which is always set via `MustInt64(0)` when the INI key is absent. So the backend will serialize a number (default 0) rather than omitting it, making the TS `undefined` case effectively unreachable with this backend. This is a type/contract inconsistency but not a clearly verifiable runtime defect in the diff by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit gives false confidence: ErrDeviceLimitReached is returned because the UPDATE matched 0 rows, not because the limit path was exercised, so the test passes even if updateDevice unconditionally fails

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, ErrDeviceLimitReached is only returned from updateDevice() when rowsAffected==0. updateDevice() is only called inside CreateOrUpdateDevice() when deviceLimit>0 and CountDevices(...) >= deviceLimit. In TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit, the first call inserts a device (no error), so the second call can only produce ErrDeviceLimitReached if the limit path was exercised and updateDevice() was invoked. The test does not pass if updateDevice “unconditionally fails” in general, because that would also fail the first insert call if it were wrongly invoked there.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Returning raw ErrDeviceLimitReached from Authenticate surfaces as a generic auth failure (likely 500/401) instead of a 429 throttling response, with no backoff or distinct status for over-limit devices

adjudication.rationale: In `pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go`, `Authenticate` now calls `TagDevice` synchronously and, on `errors.Is(err, anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached)`, returns `nil, err` directly. The diff does not show any translation of `ErrDeviceLimitReached` into a specific HTTP status (e.g., 429) or a typed/auth-specific error; it will be whatever the surrounding auth framework does with a raw error. So the finding about “generic auth failure instead of a distinct throttling response” is a grounded concern about incomplete error handling, though the exact resulting status (401/500) cannot be verified from this diff alone.
